meta.title: South Asian Partition: India–Pakistan 1947 and Bangladesh 1971
meta.scope: Research staging for the legal creation of India and Pakistan, partition of Punjab and Bengal, accession/integration of major princely states, the Kashmir dispute and ceasefire line, and East Pakistan's secession as Bangladesh.
meta.dateConvention: ISO-8601 Gregorian. Distinguish declaration, legal effectiveness, accession instrument, military control and international ceasefire line. Do not equate accession with uncontested sovereignty.
meta.mapConstraint: The current map is too coarse to represent the Radcliffe line within Punjab/Bengal or the 1949 Kashmir ceasefire line. The recommendations below are explicit whole-region fallbacks, not claims that the historical border followed the current region edges.

qualityLegend.verified: Primary legal text, UN treaty record or official government/archival source confirms the date or instrument.
qualityLegend.supported: Institutional or academic historical synthesis supports the date and interpretation.
qualityLegend.estimated: Population split is a census-based approximation used for whole-region allocation; not a precise GIS overlay.

events.title: Indian Independence Act 1947
events.note: The Act provided for two independent Dominions, India and Pakistan, from the appointed dates. The legal act is distinct from the Radcliffe boundary award and from later integration of princely states.
Pakistan became independent on 14 August 1947. East and West wings were geographically non-contiguous.
India became independent on 15 August 1947; it remained a Dominion until 26 January 1950.

events.title: Publication of the Radcliffe Awards
events.note: The Punjab and Bengal boundary awards were gazetted two days after the Dominions' independence. They split both provinces; Sylhet's referendum was a separate process. The current map does not contain enough subregions to reproduce the line.

events.title: Maharaja Hari Singh signs Instrument of Accession to India
events.note: India treats accession as legally effective; Pakistan disputes the circumstances and the final status. The whole SIK_KAS region should not be treated as uncontested Indian territory.

events.title: Junagadh administration transferred to India
events.note: The Nawab acceded to Pakistan in September 1947; Indian forces entered in November and a February 1948 referendum supported accession to India. No matching region ID was supplied; do not invent one.

events.title: Patiala and East Punjab States Union (PEPSU) formed
events.note: Patiala and several East Punjab princely states formed PEPSU, later merged into Punjab in 1956. Assign PRI_CIS to India.

events.title: Hyderabad State brought under Indian Union control
events.note: Operation Polo ended the Nizam's independent claim; the region should transfer to India from this date, with a short military-administration interval.

events.title: UN-supervised India–Pakistan ceasefire in Jammu and Kashmir
events.note: The ceasefire took effect on 1 January 1949. The Karachi Agreement of 27 July 1949 delineated the ceasefire line; this was a military line, not a final international border.

events.title: Karachi Agreement establishes the ceasefire line
events.note: UN military observers supervised the ceasefire line. The current single Kashmir/Jammu regions cannot represent the line; retain a contested status and do not split or duplicate ownership.

events.title: Travancore-Cochin Union established
events.note: Travancore and Cochin merged as a constituent state within the Indian Union; assign TRV_TRV to India.
The Constitution came into force and India became a sovereign democratic republic; universal adult suffrage was provided for.

events.title: One Unit scheme creates West Pakistan; East Bengal renamed East Pakistan
events.note: West Pakistan's provinces and princely states were amalgamated into one province; East Pakistan remained the eastern wing.
Pakistan's first Constitution came into force and ended Dominion status.
The declaration was made on 26 March; the Proclamation of Independence adopted on 10 April 1971 had effect from 26 March.

events.title: Pakistani Eastern Command surrenders in Dhaka
events.note: The surrender ended the nine-month Liberation War and established Bangladesh's effective independence. Do not use 16 December as the declaration date.

partitionDemography.allocationRecommendation: For the single Lahore-centred region SIK_LAH, assign Pakistan because Lahore lies west of the Radcliffe line. Use the 55.6/44.4 whole-province split only as contextual evidence; it is not the population share inside SIK_LAH itself.
partitionDemography.limitations: The source totals refer to the two post-award territorial portions of undivided Punjab, not to a direct population raster for the game's coarse SIK_LAH region.

partitionDemography.allocationRecommendation: If EIC_BEN must remain indivisible, assign it to Pakistan/East Pakistan because the East Bengal/East Pakistan portion held about 64.8% of the old province's population and Dhaka is the eastern-wing capital. This necessarily misassigns Calcutta/West Bengal; it is a known major map distortion, not an acceptable final border model.
partitionDemography.limitations: EIC_BEN combines Calcutta and Dacca and cannot represent the Radcliffe line. Split it into at least EIC_BEN_WEST and EIC_BEN_EAST before treating the map as historically accurate.

validationNotes: No engine region was invented. All region IDs in this package were supplied in MSG-108; blank regionIds explicitly mean the current list contains no safe mapping.
The Radcliffe line cannot be represented by the current coarse SIK_LAH and EIC_BEN regions. The recommended whole-region assignments are stopgap decisions only.

EIC_BEN assigned to East Pakistan by majority-population fallback would put Calcutta/West Bengal on the wrong side. This is a high-severity map fidelity defect; split EIC_BEN before a production historical start.
EIC_ASS remains India although Sylhet district (except Karimganj) joined East Pakistan after a referendum; this subregional transfer is not represented by EIC_ASS as a single region.

SIK_KAS and SIK_JAM are provisionally held by India for the legal accession path but must carry a contested status and a Pakistan claim. The Karachi ceasefire line is not the international border and cannot be mapped within the supplied coarse regions.
Kashmir accession is not the same as a final settlement; avoid presenting the whole princely state as uncontested Indian territory.

The 1941 population values are pre-partition census-derived estimates for post-award territories; the percentage is the share of the undivided province population, not the fraction of a game's individual coarse region.
